objectives.how: Read all 794 lines of RFC 0011 v1.3 from disk (sha1 5e40aa5f86f04e54a593f86cc5afba5d74bcc9a7) in this lens: normative language and requirement quality. Checked each line against RFC 2119 and RFC 8174 (both read in the browser on 2026-11-16) and against the requirement characteristics named in OBJ-2. Sections 3 and 6 to 7 carry nearly all defects; sections 4, 5, 8 to 10 and appendix A are informative and yielded none in this lens beyond line 42. Every quoted RFC line in the observations was copied from disk by a script that also checked each old text occurs exactly once on its stated line.

deliverables.text: This AAR: one observation and one proposal (old -> new) per defect

objectives.text: Review RFC 0011 v1.3 line by line for normative language and requirement quality: RFC 2119 as clarified by RFC 8174 (keywords in uppercase only where normative; a lowercase must, should or may in a normative clause is ambiguous); every MUST and MUST NOT names its actor and can be verified by a test or an inspection; every SHOULD says or implies when departing from it is acceptable; every requirement is singular (one obligation), unambiguous and free of vague terms (for example short, large, well within); passive voice that hides who acts; and the requirement characteristics of ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 (necessary, unambiguous, complete, singular, feasible, verifiable, correct, consistent). Report each defect with the RFC line and the exact replacement text.
objectives.how: Each defect is an observation (line, characteristic or rule violated, verbatim RFC text) with a matching proposal whose `what` is 'line <n>: <old> -> <new>'. Checks applied: lowercase key words (grep), MUST/MUST NOT without actor or test, SHOULD without a stated exception, multi-obligation sentences, vague terms ('at once', 'as it works', 'ships', 'backoff', 'structured'), passive voice that hides the actor, and internal contradictions between requirements. ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 characteristics were applied as named in this objective; the standard itself was not read (see the observation).

operational_learning.text: Check the requirements-language clause first: an RFC that adopts RFC 2119 without RFC 8174 makes every lowercase must, may and required ambiguous, so the count of lowercase key words is a quick measure of exposure.

Keep the defect table in a script that pulls each quoted line from disk and checks that each old text occurs exactly once on its stated line: line numbers and verbatim quotes are then verified, not remembered.

ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 cannot be read without purchase, and its ISO OBP preview requires accepting Terms of Use; a brief that asks for its wording should name a readable source or accept the characteristic names as given.

Most defects in this RFC are normative statements written without a key word ('the DB assigns', 'is reported at once', 'fold into'): searching for present-tense statements of behaviour in section 3 finds more defects than searching for key words.

rfis.suggestion: Yes: add `briefs/` to the CLAUDE.md Channel exception, because a long-lifecycle brief changes at each launch (3.3.1a requires a new provenance version per launching session) and a PR per launch would cost your time; then 3.3.1a can keep 'pushed to main' as written in PRO for line 316.
